chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: 'It is not permissible for the one praying to pray with one prayer except with one Takbir, except in the Funeral Prayer.'
And it is not permissible for him to pray with two prayers except in the Funeral Prayer.
And it is not permissible for him to pray with three Takbirs except in the Funeral Prayer.

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَة: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), used here to denote the opening declaration of prayer.
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ الصَّادِقُ: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the sixth Shia Imam.
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْجَنَازَةِ: The Funeral Prayer, a specific ritual prayer performed for the deceased.

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirs are in a standard prayer versus the Funeral Prayer?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that the single Takbir is the foundational norm for all prayers, with the Funeral Prayer serving as the specific exception requiring multiple Takbirs. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential principle that specific rituals (like Janazah) deviate from the general rule only when explicitly prescribed, reinforcing the structural integrity of Salah in Shia fiqh.
